boundaries: Normal training uses 20 continuing BPTT windows, each B8/L128 in chunks32, detach between updates. Stable throughput recomputed over updates3-20.
Paired checkpoint saves update20 at position2560; its two next-chunk updates use L32 and are excluded from the twenty normal timing observations.
Fresh-process restore loads the saved update20 state and actually updates another L128 window. This verifies mechanism; its own timing is not steady-state throughput.
Ledger uses a separate newly initialized model, two continuing L128 windows and intrusive saved-tensor/operator hooks. Its peaks and saved storage are not added to normal-run peaks.
Finite engineering mechanism/performance does not validate downstream learning quality. Cooperative queue admission does not control external host/device contention.
B16 has only same-process paired recovery; no fresh-interpreter B16 update and no B16 ledger were run.
Normal model seed751, input generator seed752; one fixed B/L/d input tensor is reused across the20 continuing updates. B8 is the exact first8 input samples of B16 at initialization.

Ledger model seed1107 differs from normal751; ledger input generator seed1108 differs from normal752. Fresh restore loads trained seed751 weights but generates input with1108, exactly matching ledger data only.
Training check_memory enforces sampled peak allocated48GiB only; all observed reserved peaks remain below56GiB, which is a reviewed envelope rather than a training enforcement guarantee.

Raw normal-update output-strength support is not independently paired across execution paths. Checkpoint support/metadata comparison failures are reported separately; no complete-trajectory support equivalence is inferred.

evaluation_order: Receive contents and masses for every candidate node/sample/logical position.
Prepare KV or SSD memory state and descriptors before regional allocation, over candidate rectangular rows.
Compute descriptions, regional scores and Full allocation.
Pack control>0 queries; retain nodes with any active query and pad their sample/query rectangle.
Compute selected memory output and node-independent FFN over the packed rectangle.
Publish selected rows and retain private per-node state; batched state joins/splits do not share history.

kv.history: Concatenate old+new times, weight, keys, values, features; five field banks coexist with previous state and compacted retained outputs during preparation.
kv.summary: For each original-position tile Q with bank width T, two [...,Q,T]@[...,T,s] weighted summaries, plus int64 delta/visibility, decay and denominators. This work does not shrink with m.
kv.compaction: NPU chronological prefix-count/cumsum/scatter partition; CPU stable timestamp argsort; gather all five fields into retained finite slots. No float timestamp conversion.
kv.full_linear_multiply_adds: Rfull*(2*d*m+3*d*f), before attention, normalization, RoPE and adapter terms
kv.attention: m/32 heads; original logical query tiles and int64 window masks; semantically effective pairs and rectangle operand pairs are distinct.
kv.conclusion: Narrow m reduces Q/K/V projection and cache payload, while summary width, window/control work, content width and FFN stay fixed. Retained cache payload does not predict peak memory or whole-model speed.

ssd.prepare_operations: All candidate rows undergo gate/projected/dt input projection, d-to-s summary, logical four-tap convolution over d+64 channels, h-by-32-by-32 state scan, summary scan, and d-to-s read projection before Full selection.
ssd.persistent_payload_excluding_conv_fp32_b: 4*(h*32*32+2*s+2)+8 per node/sample; convolution retains its own bounded private int64-time/value cache
ssd.conclusion: SSD finite state reduces persistent history size, but preparation remains a pre-allocation cost. Prefix/doubling choices affect intermediate and saved storage; do not treat all SSD work as selected-only.

packing_ffn.padding_ratio: executed_rows/selected_rows, separately by memory kind and original query tile
packing_ffn.ffn_multiply_adds: 3*d*f*executed_rows; FFN parameters remain node-independent in memory_shared candidate
packing_ffn.boundary: KV packs per original query tile; SSD packs its entire finish window. Increased region batching may reduce dispatch and increase rectangular padding.

shared_memory.formula: W_node=W_region+L_node@R_node for each shared memory NodeLinear, including the SSD input projection that emits the d-channel output gate; state remains private. SSD NodeVector parameters a_log, dt_bias, skip, rho, conv_kernel and conv_bias are regional bases with no low-rank adapters. FFN/reception/description ownership remains independent.
shared_memory.adapter_multiply_adds: rows*r*(in+out) for each mathematical NodeLinear. HeadQuery retains one adapter per head; query adapter sum is rows*r*((m/32)*d+m), not one merged rank-r adapter.
shared_memory.uniform_boundary: Uniformity uses static possible-owner metadata; arbitrary dynamic selections conservatively retain BMM unless all possible owners share one base.
shared_memory.conclusion: Mixed-region batches repeat gathered bases per node row; they are not automatically regrouped into one large GEMM per regional owner. Parameter storage reduction is not arithmetic or bandwidth reduction. Runtime matrix operands and node_matrix_dispatch provide separate evidence.

units.throughput: independent input positions/s; complete sequence throughput = B/complete request seconds

limitations: Finite initial weights and full-schedule diagnostic outputs/private state are checked. Normal and cold samples contain finite timing/allocation metadata, but their output tensors were not separately checked in timed regions.
Actual readout, returned values/strengths and retained floating state are FP32; state includes int64. FP32 operator arithmetic is the recorded policy, not a new per-operator trace in this audit.
First backbone output maps independent support-witness flags to timed ready boundaries. It excludes import, construction and transfer, has no task head and is not full language-model TTFT.
Stable decode excludes the first incremental call: denominator B*(decode_steps-1). Complete independent sequence throughput is B/complete_seconds, not a token or padding denominator.

Same configuration and seed require the same initial parameter identity across B. Input generation uses full batch/length shapes: equal seed alone does not imply identical trajectory when schedule length or batch changes.

Cold and normal peaks are checked separately against48/56GiB; intrusive diagnostic peaks and unrecorded warmup peaks are outside these checks. No claim about physical capacity maxima or global best batch.
Source/card/raw file identities remain attached to each point. Frozen source and descendant terminal verification belong to the separate final release audit.
